# Delivery performance decides whether customers come back — and what they say when they do. {.hero}

I measured it, I predicted it, and I read what customers actually wrote. All three
projects run on the same Olist dataset — around 100,000 orders across nine related
tables — and each one ships a written analysis, a one-page decision memo, and an
honest account of what the data cannot support.

## Projects

<div class="projects">

<article class="project">
<div class="project-seq">01<span class="project-status status-published">Published</span></div>
<div class="project-detail">
<h3>Which levers actually move customer satisfaction and repeat purchase?</h3>

<p class="project-stack">PostgreSQL, dbt, SQL, Python, Quarto</p>

## How this is built

Every project here runs from a clean clone.

```bash
uv run python tasks.py setup      # dependencies + database + dataset
uv run python tasks.py pipeline   # load, build, charts, tests, render
```

The dataset comes from a revision-pinned mirror and is checked against expected
file sizes on download, so the numbers cannot change quietly underneath you.
